evidence.claim: The assumed Gaussian functional form for the N-S primary beam is weakly justified and inconsistent with independent data, with systematic deviations ignored in favor of an oversimplified model.
evidence.excerpt: The assumed Gaussian functional form for the N-S primary beam (Eq. (2)) is weakly justified and appears inconsistent with independent data. The comparison with drone-based measurements (Fig. 11) shows clear, systematic deviations from a Gaussian shape, yet this is primarily blamed on drone systematics rather than questioning the model's validity.

judge_panel.reason: The paper acknowledges that 'the drone measured beam can deviate significantly from the Gaussian shape' and attributes this to drone systematics, while also noting 'it is possible that the actual beam shape intrinsically deviates from our model.' The Gaussian model is justified by reference to Yu et al. (2023) and EM simulations, but the systematic deviations in Fig. 11 are not fully quantitatively resolved, making it genuinely unclear whether the model or the drone is the primary source of discrepancy.

The Gaussian N-S model is explicitly justified by prior work: "We assume the beam factor along the North-South direction has a Gaussian form (Yu et al. 2023)" and "This model approximates the results obtained from the electromagnetic (EM) field simulation by Sun et al. (2022), as thoroughly validated in the work of Yu et al. (2023)." The paper also does not ignore discrepancies with the drone data, stating "it is possible that the actual beam shape intrinsically deviates from our model, which only captures a general profile."

The authors observe that 'the drone measured beam can deviate significantly from the Gaussian shape', but they primarily attribute this to 'errors inherent in the drone-based methodology' and retain their simplified Gaussian model.
